newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS SOLID BUT WOULD WELCOME CORRECTION.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS SOLID BUT WOULD WELCOME CORRECTION.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds remained well-supported on Tuesday with little immediate danger expected from U.S. CPI data for May or the Amsterdam summit but traders said they were hoping for a correction soon to revive business.
"It's a disaster...with a benchmark yield at 5.75 percent people prefer to shun the market. Basically, all we see is some interbanking (trade)," one trader said.

But a correction was unlikely soon with U.S. Consumer Price Index data for May, due at 1230 GMT, set to be soft and good for bonds, and the Amsterdam EU summit expected to yield nothing but positive news for EMU.
"But the data can't continue to be good," one trader noted. "Perhaps the balloon has now been inflated too much."
Kredietbank said in its daily comment that given the oversold technicals, it remained in favour of selling into any rally occurring after the data.
ABN-AMRO added that as long as Treasuries continued to rally, it would be difficult to see Europe much lower. OLOs were still rock steady in spread against Bunds.
The 10-year OLO/Bund spread narrowed to seven basis points from nine early on Monday.
"There is still a fair amount of strong bids in OLOs, which explains the lower yield," one trader said.
Another said he believed the market was now at the bottom of the yield spread range and it would widen again once the dust had settled after the EU summit.
Banque Degroof Luxembourg said it believed that enthusiasm in the market was likely to cool down in the next weeks.
